records.candidate_name: Petite rivière de la Baleine system (Nunavik)
records.supported_name_scope: Petite rivière de la Baleine identifies the long westward river and the representative connected system. The eastern feeder and individual lake passages retain bounded, separately described scope; regional cartography does not assign exact hydronym transitions.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual eastern east–north–west hook, westward lake-country approach, marked southward bend, long west-to-northwest trunk and coastal ending south of Lac Guillaume-Delisle jointly correspond to Petite rivière de la Baleine. The selection does not turn north along the Nastapoka route or follow the Grande rivière de la Baleine farther south.
records.region: Nunavik, Nord-du-Québec, Canada: eastern lake country south of the Nastapoka system, continuing west to the eastern Hudson Bay coast north of Kuujjuarapik.
records.completion_scope: Completed for bounded representative-system identity using actual CEHQ regional-map pixels, the official Tursujuq map and an independent hydrological-study scope check. The initial feeder’s individual name, the exact sequence and entry/exit vertices of small eastern waterbodies, and a surveyed mouth or tidal limit remain unassigned. Those limits do not prevent identification of the connected representative corridor.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Nunavik is an editorial disambiguator, not an added part of the hydronym.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Actual eastward, northward and westward headwater hook followed by the westward lake-country approach. The initial feeder and exact small-waterbody sequence remain unassigned; the modeled beginning is not replaced by a better-known nearby lake or northern branch.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: D’Iberville, Amichinatwayach, Kaminapiskwasi, Sirvé, Mondain, Petit lac des Loups Marins and Lac à l’Eau Claire are separately labeled regional waterbodies. Their proximity or drainage association is not used to assert that the selected line traverses each lake. D’Iberville and Petit lac des Loups Marins lie in the neighboring northern lake setting. Exact named-lake passages and transition vertices on the eastern selected corridor remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: All three selected pieces are modeled as mainstem; there are no separately selected non-mainstem pieces. Boutin is a separately mapped branch. The hydrological study’s natural secondary connections mean that representative routing should not be equated with complete or exclusive drainage membership.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Northwest-turning lower river toward Hudson Bay south of the Lac Guillaume-Delisle/Le Goulet setting. The precise surveyed mouth, freshwater–tidal transition, estuarine channels and offshore continuation are not established.
naming_scope_details.historical_source_scope: The INRS report is a 1979 hydrological study that also analyzes proposed developments. Only its natural-basin map and secondary-outflow discussion are used. Proposed reservoirs and diversions are not treated as built infrastructure or current operating conditions.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Fragment boundaries and mainstem membership do not establish official naming boundaries; model length is not an official natural-river length. No formal naming date, Indigenous-name equivalence, historical alias series, current protection-status determination or Korean form is established.

records.supported_name_scope: Rivière Nastapoka identifies the connecting river system and its long westward to northwestward trunk downstream of the Loups Marins lake country. The initial feeder, separately named lakes and terminal transition retain bounded scopes.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The actual selected eastern-to-southern headwater loop, reversal north through the Petit lac des Loups Marins setting, westward passage across Lacs des Loups Marins, southwest-then-northwest trunk bend, Natwakupaw passage and coastal endpoint jointly distinguish this selection from the Petite rivière de la Baleine corridor farther south and the separate routes into Lac Guillaume-Delisle. This distinguishes the selected routes without assuming that adjacent drainage systems are hydrologically isolated.
records.region: Nunavik, Nord-du-Québec, Canada, from the eastern Loups Marins lake country to the eastern Hudson Bay coast north of Umiujaq.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence from the actual two selected pieces, using readable primary-map pixels and supporting regional hydrology prose. Exact feeder naming, small connecting-channel names, lake entry/exit vertices, the first officially named Nastapoka point and surveyed mouth or tidal limits remain unassigned. These scope limits do not prevent representative identity. No software work, tests, audits, geometry-validation stage or publication was performed.

naming_scope_details.geographic_qualifier: Nunavik is an editorial disambiguator, not part of the official river name.
naming_scope_details.upper_scope: The modeled beginning includes an eastern feeder and a pronounced southward loop before the northward D’Iberville–Petit lac des Loups Marins approach. The first feeder and small lake names are not assigned. The maps support the lake-country correspondence at regional scale, not individual entry and exit vertices.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Lac D’Iberville, Petit lac des Loups Marins, Lacs des Loups Marins and Lac Natwakupaw retain separately mapped waterbody scopes. No lake name is treated as a river alias. Lac Bourdel is context for a northern contribution, not the selected initial route.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Both selected pieces are modeled mainstem pieces. This does not make the initial feeder or every interlake channel officially Nastapoka. The southern neighboring river routes are distinguishable in the maps, but reported secondary outflows prevent an assertion of entirely isolated drainage basins.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Nastapoka’s Hudson Bay coastal approach north of Umiujaq; no extension through the sea, exact estuary delineation or tidal-limit assignment.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Modeled mainstem membership and fragment boundaries do not establish legal hydronym boundaries. Rendered model length is not an official river length. No formal naming date, historical alias series, Indigenous-name equivalence, Korean form, exact basin boundary, current cross-basin discharge or present-day protection status is established. The INRS spelling Nastapoca is reported only as source usage, not adopted as an accepted alias.

records.candidate_name: Sevier River system (East Fork–Sevier Lake corridor)
records.supported_name_scope: East Fork of the Sevier River is supported for the southern branch, with Sevier River for the downstream trunk. Reservoir passages and the terminal lake/playa remain distinct naming scopes; no uniform river name is assigned to every modeled segment.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The complete single selected mainstem follows the eastern headwater branch, turns west near Antimony/Kingston, continues north through Piute and the central Sevier valleys, bends west below Sevier Bridge Reservoir, and passes the Delta setting toward Sevier Lake. The separate Hatch–Panguitch source route is not the selected southern approach.
records.region: Central and south-central Utah, United States, from the Paunsaugunt/Bryce Canyon headwater region north through the Sevier valleys, then west and southwest into the Sevier Desert.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence using readable official basin-map pixels, a hydrologic sub-area map and supporting basin description. Exact first feeder, river/reservoir boundaries and terminal lake-entry vertices remain unassigned. No further source acquisition is pending for this assessment.

naming_scope_details.upper_scope: East Fork of the Sevier River branch, including the Tropic Reservoir setting. No exact starting feeder or name-transition vertex is assigned. Asay Creek, Mammoth Creek and the Hatch–Panguitch branch retain separate scope.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_scope: The selected corridor intersects reservoir settings, especially Tropic, Piute, Sevier Bridge and the lower Delta-area storage system. The basin maps support their regional sequence, not exact shoreline, dam or reservoir-to-river transition vertices.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Otter Creek and San Pitch River are separately mapped contributions, not aliases for the full selected object.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Northern Sevier Lake/playa approach. Neither the entire lake nor the modeled final segment is assigned a river hydronym; no exact contemporary shoreline or wet/dry extent is asserted.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: One modeled mainstem fragment does not establish one hydronym, permanent surface flow or an official source-to-mouth length. The 1999 map is historical planning cartography, not evidence of present reservoir operations or lake inundation. No Korean form or historical name sequence was established.

records.supported_name_scope: Río Loa supports the representative identity of the selected U-shaped corridor. The exact initial feeder, impoundment limits and surveyed mouth vertex remain unassigned. San Pedro, Salado and San Salvador are separate contributing rivers.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The entire single selected line was inspected. Its long southward eastern arm, westward southern turn, northward western arm and final westward coastal reach correspond to the complete Loa course described by DGA. Readable Figure 2.1 supplies middle-basin cartographic context; it does not cover the extreme source and mouth.
records.region: Northern Chile: upper Andean Loa corridor, Chiuchiu–Calama, Chacance–Quillagua and the Pacific coastal approach at Caleta Huelén.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative correspondence from the whole selected path, DGA’s complete course description and its readable middle-basin map. This is not an assertion that every endpoint was matched to detailed map pixels. Exact headmost-feeder and mouth naming limits remain unassigned; further acquisition is not pending for the representative identity.

naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Upper Loa corridor; exact initial feeder and natural-source vertex unassigned.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: San Pedro, Salado and San Salvador remain distinct tributaries, not aliases of the selected line.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_scope: DGA’s segmentation distinguishes the Conchi dam and outlet context along the corridor; no current shoreline or exact river–reservoir transition is assigned.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Pacific coastal approach associated with Caleta Huelén; exact mouth and tidal boundary unassigned.
naming_scope_details.evidence_limit: The full course is supported by DGA prose and the route’s distinctive directional sequence; the acquired mapped figure covers only the central basin. No claim of detailed pixel correspondence at every endpoint is made.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: A single mainstem fragment and model length do not establish uniform hydronym limits, a natural-river length or present flow conditions.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
